explain.say: A biomass power station burns plant material, such as wood pellets, straw or energy crops. While those plants were growing, they took carbon dioxide out of the air to build their leaves and wood.

explain.say: If new plants grow to replace what was burned, they soak up that carbon dioxide again. That loop is why biomass is called carbon neutral, unlike coal, whose carbon was locked away for millions of years.

explain.say: But the loop takes time. A tree may take decades to regrow, and harvesting, drying and shipping pellets use energy too. So biomass is only low carbon if forests are well managed and replanted.

faq.q: How do plants take in carbon?
faq.a: By photosynthesis: leaves take in carbon dioxide and use sunlight's energy to turn it into sugars, which build the plant's wood and leaves. About half the dry weight of wood is carbon.
asks: Where does the carbon in wood come from?

faq.a: Small cylinders of dried, compressed sawdust and wood waste. Pressing makes them dense, dry and easy to ship and burn evenly, so big stations like Drax in England burn millions of tonnes a year.
asks: Why burn pellets instead of logs?

faq.q: Why is coal not carbon neutral?
faq.a: Coal's carbon was taken from the air by plants around 300 million years ago and buried. Burning it adds that ancient carbon to today's air, with nothing growing to take it back.
asks: What is the difference between biomass and coal?

faq.a: Only over time, and only if the forest regrows. Burning wood releases carbon dioxide at once, while regrowing trees take decades to absorb it, and harvesting and transport add more. Scientists still debate how green large-scale biomass is.
asks: Is burning wood bad for the climate?

faq.a: Bioenergy with carbon capture and storage: a biomass power station catches the carbon dioxide from its chimney and stores it deep underground. Because the plants took that carbon from the air, this could remove carbon dioxide overall.
asks: Can biomass remove carbon from the air?

facts: About half the dry mass of wood is carbon.
Drax power station in North Yorkshire converted four of its six coal-fired units to burn wood pellets.

quiz.say: What makes biomass different from coal in the carbon cycle?

options.show: Its carbon was taken from the air recently by growing plants
options.say: Its carbon was taken from the air recently by growing plants

options.show: Burning it releases no carbon dioxide
options.say: Burning it releases no carbon dioxide

quiz.why: Biomass carbon was absorbed by plants recently and can be taken up again by regrowth, whereas coal's carbon was buried for millions of years.

wrong.1: Burning biomass does release carbon dioxide; regrowth is what takes it back.
wrong.2: Coal comes from underground; biomass is grown on the surface.
